originality.rationale: Explicit two-coordinate family x=(1,0), y_b=(b,1) gives denominators D_p(b)=1+(1+|b|^p)^(2/p)-((1-b)^p+1)^(2/p). For p>2, D_p(-1)<0<D_p(0), and N_p=1+(1+|b|^p)^(2/p)-((1+b)^p+1)^(2/p) is positive at a negative-b zero; approach from D>0 gives +infinity. For 1<=p<2, D_p(0)<0<D_p(1) and N_p<0 at a positive-b zero; approach from D<0 gives +infinity. At p=infinity D=2-(1-b)^2, N=1 and b approaches 1-sqrt(2) from above; Hilbert parallelogram law makes the quotient identically -1 when defined. The two-coordinate embedding proves arbitrary |I|>=2, no reliance on sampled exponents.
